DI G Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue West Triangle, Quezon City 1100 DILG Legal Opinion No. 49 S. 2015 .1 1 DEC HON. RUBEN M. SAYO Acting Mayor Municipality of Aritao Province of Nueva Vizcaya Dear Acting Mayor Sayo: We write concerning your 08 July 2015 letter requesting this Department's guidance/opinion on how to protect the interest of a government project from a private investment project duly covered by a Memorandum of Agreement with the Municipality. As represented in your aforesaid letter, the Manager of Balibago Waterworks will be drilling a 200-meter deep well from a source located at a mere 100-meter distance from the point source of CUWASA water system, a government water supply project benefitting 325 households and 1 ,972 population. As a reaction thereto, the Sangguniang Barangay of Cutar, Aritao, Nueva Vizcaya and CUWASA officials adopted Resolution No. 2015-13 entitled "A JOINT RESOLUTION OF BARANGAY COUNCIL AND CUWASA OFFICIALS PLEADING THE NON- ISSUANCE OF NECESSARY CERTIFICATES AND CLEARANCES FOR BALIBAGO TO EXTRACT WATER AT BARANGAY CUTAR," pertinent portion of which reads: "WHEREAS, to protect and to sustain the efficient supply of potable water, we believe that no other huge water system extracting big volume of water should be constructed in the area; WHEREAS, the Barangay Council and CUVVASA jointly appeal that the BALIBAGO Project be relocated so as not to cause adverse effect to the present project; FURTHER, the Barangay Council and CUWASA plead to the Hon. Mayor Lucita L. Tan not to issue clearances and permit for Balibago's water extraction project. " Hence, your request for guidance/opinion. It may be well to stress at the outset that Mayor Lucita L. Tan of Aritao, Nueva Vizcaya came to the Department informing us that the issuance of the "necessary certificates and clearances" required before Balibago Waterworks could start its drilling activity, subject of Resolution No. 2015-13, is governed by an ordinance and/or guidelines

duly issued by the municipal government of Aritao. The Department was not however furnished with a copy of such ordinance and/or guidelines in order for us to examine the requirements and/or conditions, if there be any, for the issuance of said certificates and clearances. Be that as it may, there being an ordinance and/or guidelines duly issued by the municipal government of Aritao governing the issuance of such necessary certificates and clearances needed by Balibago Waterworks before it could start its drilling activity in the area, the same should govern the issuance thereof. In this regard, please be reminded that the local chief executive (LCE) of a local government unit (LGU) is mandated under Section 444 (b)(2) of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 to: "SECTION 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensa tion. —xxx (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: (2) Enforce all laws and ordinances relative to the governance of and the exercise of its corporate powers provided for under Section 22 of this Code, implement all approved policies, programs, projects, services and activities of the municipality xxx" Assuming that the Balibago Waterworks complied with all the requisites and/or conditions set forth in the ordinance and/or guidelines duly issued by the municipal government of Aritao, we note that the Sangguniang Barangay of Cutar together with the CUWASA officials adopted Resolution No. 2015-13 expressing their apprehension that the drilling project of the Balibago Waterworks might cause adverse effect to CUWASA water system, an existing government water supply project in the area. At this juncture, please be reminded that a Resolution, such as Resolution No. 2015-13 adopted by the Sangguniang Barangay of Cutar together with the CUWASA officials, is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a lawmaking body on a specific matterl , and therefore not a law which the LCE shall mandatorily enforce. Further, it appears that such apprehension of the Sangguniang Barangay of Cutar and the CUWASA officials as embodied in their Resolution No. 2015-13 is not supported by a finding from an actual study conducted by a competent authority (e.g. Municipal Engineer) stating that the drilling of a 200-meter deep well from a source located at a mere 100-meter distance from another point source would necessarily affect the latter I Municipality of Parafiaque vs. V.M. Realty Corporation, G.R. No. 127820, 20 July 1998.

point source. Hence, it is suggested that an actual study be conducted first for this purpose as there might be a possibility that the two (2) projects can co-exist. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Ve truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary DILGOUSLG 2015 4 201727 Is/17 Copy furnished: DIR. MARLO L IRINGAN Officer- in -Charge DILG-Region 11 Carig, Tuguegarao City Cagayan
